title: Agreement of multisection component loci near a connected fibre
statement:
Let $f:X\to B$ and $p:Z\to B$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\sigma:Z\to X$ satisfy $f\circ\sigma=p$. Suppose $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with geometrically reduced fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Put $Y=X\times_B Z$ with projection $g:Y\to Z$ and section $s=(\sigma,\mathrm{id}_Z)$ [def-pc-base-change]. Define $C\subseteq Y$ to be the union, over $z\in Z$, of the connected component of $s(z)$ in $Y_z$ [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Put $R=Z\times_B Z$, let $q:R\to B$ be its structure morphism, let $a_i:X\times_B R\to Y$ be induced by the two projections $R\to Z$, let $h:X\times_B R\to R$ be the projection, and let $s_i:R\to X\times_B R$ be the two induced sections. Then $C$ is open [def-weil-open-immersion], and $a_i^{-1}C$ is the section-component locus of $s_i$ for $i=0,1$. For every $b_0\in B$ with $X_{b_0}$ geometrically connected over $\kappa(b_0)$ [def-weil-residue-field], there is an open $W\subseteq R$ containing $q^{-1}(b_0)$ such that $s_0(W)\subseteq a_1^{-1}C$, $s_1(W)\subseteq a_0^{-1}C$, and
$$h^{-1}W\cap a_0^{-1}C=h^{-1}W\cap a_1^{-1}C.$$
No finiteness or surjectivity hypothesis on $p$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof from formation of X_Z through mutual section incidence and equality over W.

proof.text: Base change along $p$ makes $g:Y\to Z$ flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For $z\in Z$, put $b=p(z)$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $Y_z$ with $X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\kappa(z)$: both represent compatible maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ over $B$. Any further field extension $L/\kappa(z)$ gives $Y_z\times_{\kappa(z)}L=X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}L$, which is reduced by the assumed geometric reducedness of $X_b$. Thus every fibre of $g$ is geometrically reduced. The equations $f\sigma=p$ and $g s=\mathrm{id}_Z$ identify $s$ as the required section.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, first base-change paragraph; morphisms.tex Tags 01U9 and 01TS

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-reduced-section-component-open] to $(g,s)$ using step 1. Its component locus is exactly $C$, so $C$ is open. For $i=0,1$, the square with maps $(a_i,h,g,\operatorname{pr}_i)$ is cartesian by [def-pc-base-change], and $a_i s_i=s\operatorname{pr}_i$. Also $g$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Indeed, let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$ be affine and $y\in g^{-1}(V)$. By [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] there are affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A'\ni y$ and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $g(U)\subseteq V'$ and $R\to A'$ of finite presentation, hence finitely generated by the displayed variables. Choose $c\in A$ with $g(y)\in D(c)\subseteq V\cap V'$ and $D(c)=D(c')$ for some $c'\in R$ (opens standard in both affines form a basis of $V\cap V'$). Then $U\cap g^{-1}D(c)=\operatorname{Spec}A'_{c'}$ with $A'_{c'}$ finitely generated over $R_{c'}=A_c$, hence over $A$ (add $1/c$). These affines cover $g^{-1}(V)$. Hence [lem-sbc-section-component-cartesian] applies and gives $C_i:=a_i^{-1}C=C(h,s_i)$. Both $C_i$ are open by continuity of $a_i$.

source.place: Tag 057I, construction of the two open loci; Tags 055R and 055M

proof.text: Fix $r\in q^{-1}(b_0)$. The same fibre-product identification as in step 1 gives $h^{-1}(r)=X_{b_0}\times_{\kappa(b_0)}\kappa(r)$, with underlying fibre subspace as in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. This fibre is connected by geometric connectedness of $X_{b_0}$. It contains both section points $s_0(r),s_1(r)$, so each of their connected components is the whole fibre. Consequently $s_0(r)\in C_1$ and $s_1(r)\in C_0$.

source.place: Tag 057I, paragraph beginning Let (Z times_Y Z)_y

proof.text: Set $W=s_0^{-1}(C_1)\cap s_1^{-1}(C_0)$. Since $C_0,C_1$ are open and sections are continuous, $W$ is open. Step 3 shows $q^{-1}(b_0)\subseteq W$. Its definition gives $s_0(W)\subseteq C_1$ and $s_1(W)\subseteq C_0$. This construction works even if $q^{-1}(b_0)$ is empty or infinite.

source.place: Tag 057I, mutual section incidence and construction of W

proof.text: For $r\in W$, write $D_i$ for the connected component of $s_i(r)$ in $h^{-1}(r)$. The incidence in step 4 gives $s_0(r)\in D_1$, while $s_0(r)\in D_0$, so $D_0,D_1$ intersect. Their union is connected: in any separation of the union each connected $D_i$ lies wholly on one side, and their common point forces the same side. Maximality of each connected component therefore gives $D_0=D_1$. Since step 2 identifies $C_i\cap h^{-1}(r)$ with $D_i$, a point over $W$ lies in $C_0$ exactly when it lies in $C_1$. Taking the union over $r\in W$ proves $h^{-1}W\cap a_0^{-1}C=h^{-1}W\cap a_1^{-1}C$.

lean.statement: theorem multisection_component_overlap_neighbourhood {X B Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ B) (p : Z ⟶ B) (σ : Z ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = p) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (hred : ∀ b : B, GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField b)) : IsOpen (multisectionComponentLocus f p σ hσ) ∧ (∀ i : Fin 2, multisectionOverlapMap f p i ⁻¹' multisectionComponentLocus f p σ hσ = {x : ↥(pullback f (pullback.fst p p ≫ p)) | x ∈ connectedComponentIn (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst p p ≫ p) ⁻¹' {pullback.snd f (pullback.fst p p ≫ p) x}) (multisectionOverlapSection f p σ hσ i (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst p p ≫ p) x))}) ∧ ∀ b₀ : B, GeometricallyConnected (f.fiberToSpecResidueField b₀) → ∃ W : (pullback p p).Opens, (pullback.fst p p ≫ p) ⁻¹' {b₀} ⊆ (W : Set ↥(pullback p p)) ∧ multisectionOverlapSection f p σ hσ 0 '' (W : Set ↥(pullback p p)) ⊆ multisectionOverlapMap f p 1 ⁻¹' multisectionComponentLocus f p σ hσ ∧ multisectionOverlapSection f p σ hσ 1 '' (W : Set ↥(pullback p p)) ⊆ multisectionOverlapMap f p 0 ⁻¹' multisectionComponentLocus f p σ hσ ∧ (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst p p ≫ p) ⁻¹' (W : Set ↥(pullback p p))) ∩ (multisectionOverlapMap f p 0 ⁻¹' multisectionComponentLocus f p σ hσ) = (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst p p ≫ p) ⁻¹' (W : Set ↥(pullback p p))) ∩ (multisectionOverlapMap f p 1 ⁻¹' multisectionComponentLocus f p σ hσ)
